newsitem.title: FRANCE: ICC launches business campaign against corruption.
newsitem.headline: ICC launches business campaign against corruption.

text.p: The International Chamber of Commerce (ICC) said on Wednesday it was drawing up a guide to help companies comply with its new rules to fight business corruption.
"We're working out a programme to help management to implement it," a spokesman for the Paris-based lobby group said. "We will be issuing the guide to thousands of companies."

The group said ICC business leaders and experts were working on the guide for corporate compliance programmes in companies that adopt the ICC code of conduct announced last March, prohibiting extortion and bribery.
The ICC is made up of more than 7,000 member companies and business associations in 130 countries and lobbies for free trade and private enterprise worldwide.

The ICC said its code was only a first step toward combating corruption. "To make sure the code of conduct effectively controls corporate behaviour will depend on the compliance programme conducted by management," said Fritz Heimann, a senior counsel with General Electric Co.

Heimann, speaking for the ICC, said while business leaders wanted an end to corruption in international business, many companies were reluctant to act unilaterally if they believed their competitors would continue to pay bribes.
"Only by developing a broad consensus can the reluctance to act individually be overcome," he said

The ICC said extortion and bribery were not only morally wrong, they had a "profoundly distorting effect on the world economy, rewarding inefficiency, reducing competition and diverting resources into non-productive sectors".
